candidates.title: Low-stakes weekly quizzing and long-term retention in undergraduate physics
candidates.snippet: In a crossover design across two sections of an algebra-based physics course (n = 236), topics practiced with weekly low-stakes quizzes were retained better on a delayed test given eight weeks later than topics practiced with worked-example review (61% vs. 52% correct). candidates.title: Retrieval practice in middle school science classrooms
candidates.snippet: Seventh- and eighth-grade science students (n = 540) completed clicker-based retrieval practice at the start of each lesson. Unit test scores were 7 percentage points higher for quizzed than for non-quizzed content.

candidates.title: The testing effect in college classrooms: a meta-analysis
candidates.snippet: We meta-analyzed 118 effect sizes from classroom studies of retrieval practice in higher education. Retrieval practice produced a moderate overall benefit on course assessments (g = 0.47). Effects were larger when feedback was given and when the final test was delayed.
